launch_attempts.attention_backend_selected: FLASHINFER (vllm built-in MLA kernel, not python flashinfer package)
launch_attempts.root_cause: VLLM_CUTLASS NVFP4 linear GEMM kernel was compiled for sm_100 (B100/B200). The B300 is sm_103. sm_103 is not in torch compiled arch list. Pre-compiled sm_100 kernels crash at runtime on sm_103. TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.0a has no effect on pre-compiled kernels (no nvcc for JIT). PTX fallback would need compute_103 or sm_103 PTX which is absent.

sm_103_architecture_analysis.gap: sm_103 (B300 SXM6) sits between sm_100 (B100/B200) and sm_120 (GB200/Rubin). Neither compiled arch runs correctly on sm_103.
sm_103_architecture_analysis.ptx_fallback: compute_120 PTX is too new for sm_103 JIT. sm_100 compiled code fails at kernel execution.
sm_103_architecture_analysis.torch_cuda_arch_list_env_effect: TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.0a only governs JIT compilation via nvcc. nvcc absent, so env var has zero effect.

flashinfer_analysis.root_cause: No nvcc binary and no flashinfer-cubin package. All FlashInfer backends gated behind has_flashinfer()=False.
flashinfer_analysis.note: trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe IS importable from flashinfer.fused_moe directly, but vllm's has_flashinfer_moe() gates on nvcc/cubin. Attention backend is different: uses vllm's compiled MLA kernel (flash_mla_with_kvcache in _custom_ops), not the python flashinfer package — so FLASHINFER attention backend name is misleading; it actually ran vllm's internal FlashMLA implementation which IS compiled.
